To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

confidence intervals are a fundamental tool in parameter estimation and that the SOCR tools provide an effective, accessible, interactive and dynamic computational library of statistical tools for confidence intervals.
confidence intervals provide an important and flexible mechanism to summarize and communicate uncertainty about population parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, deployment and use of the web-based tools and resources for the efficient and reliable simulation and estimation of confidence intervals.

the development of a novel computational library for constructing confidence intervals, and the demonstration of its use in the estimation of the US unemployment rate as well as in the estimation of hippocampal surfaces.

the development of a new, interactive, dynamic and open-source web-based computational library of statistical methods for confidence interval estimation, as well as the development of new SOCR resources that utilize this library.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

confidence intervals are fundamental and common approaches for parameter estimation and hypothesis testing, and the SOCR applet provides a useful computational tool to understand and explore the effect of various assumptions and parameters on the resulting confidence interval estimates.
confidence intervals, computed and interpreted properly, are an indispensable component in a wide range of scientific researches, applications and experiments.
confidence intervals provide a way to measure how reliable an estimate is and they indicate the range of plausible values for an unknown population parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the confidence intervals are the main workhorse for statistically-grounded decision making, and that there is no reason to avoid modern computational algorithms for confidence interval computations, especially for complex models.
the confidence interval applet is a useful and accessible computational resource for the understanding and analysis of confidence intervals.
the new SOCR applets are useful for understanding and interpreting confidence intervals, and they can be used in the teaching, research and presentation settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
confidence intervals are essential in the general practice of statistics and data analysis, and are not just theoretical concepts.
confidence interval estimation provides a robust, computationally-tractabel and reliable approach to parameter estimation.
the SOCR applets can be effectively used for interactive, empirical exploration and investigation of the effects of the various parameter estimators and confidence levels on the confidence intervals.
